explanations.explanation: That's the word the writer uses: Judah was exiled to Babylon "…because of their unfaithfulness." (1 Chronicles 9:1) The writer says it plainly and doesn't dress it up. I think it's a hard line to read, so I'll just say it's heavy and leave it there.

Poverty is a fair guess, friend, but it's not what the text says. The writer says Judah was exiled to Babylon "…because of their unfaithfulness." (1 Chronicles 9:1) Nothing there mentions money, so the answer is unfaithfulness.

Weakness sounds like a reasonable answer, but the writer never gives it. He says Judah was exiled to Babylon "…because of their unfaithfulness." (1 Chronicles 9:1) The reason is about faithfulness, not strength.

Yes! The first to resettle their own property in their cities were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants. (1 Chronicles 9:2) So the people who served at the house of God were among the first ones back. The story didn't stay in Babylon.

Good guess, but kings and princes aren't on the list. The text names Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants as the first to resettle. (1 Chronicles 9:2) So the answer is the priests and Levites, and this verse doesn't mention a king at all.

Prophets and judges are big names in the Bible, but this verse doesn't list them. It says the first to resettle were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants. (1 Chronicles 9:2) That makes priests and Levites the answer.

Not quite, friend. The text says Shallum and his relatives were assigned to guard the thresholds of the Tent "…just as their fathers had been assigned to guard the entrance to the dwelling of the LORD." (1 Chronicles 9:19) So their fathers had this job before them. It's a family tradition, not a new gig.

False is right! Shallum and his relatives were assigned to guard the thresholds of the Tent "…just as their fathers had been assigned to guard the entrance to the dwelling of the LORD." (1 Chronicles 9:19) Their fathers had been assigned this very kind of guarding before them. So it's not a brand new job, it's a family tradition.

That's the one. The writer says Phinehas son of Eleazar had been in charge of the gatekeepers, "…and the LORD was with him." (1 Chronicles 9:20) Of everything the writer could say about a man, that's the line he picked. I'd take it over any title.

Nice try, but the writer never says Phinehas built a single gate. He says Phinehas had been in charge of the gatekeepers, and "…the LORD was with him." (1 Chronicles 9:20) Being in charge of the gatekeepers is a different job from building anything.

This is a name-heavy chapter, so I get why you'd pick it. But the writer doesn't say Phinehas wrote down names. He says Phinehas was in charge of the gatekeepers, and "…the LORD was with him." (1 Chronicles 9:20)

Yes, trust! David and Samuel the seer "…had appointed them to their positions of trust." (1 Chronicles 9:22) A seer is someone who sees. These gatekeepers were trusted with the doors of the house of the LORD, and that's no small thing.

Wealth is a fun guess, but the text doesn't say it. David and Samuel the seer "…had appointed them to their positions of trust." (1 Chronicles 9:22) The word is trust, because these men were trusted with the doors.

Comfort sounds nice, friend, but it's not in the verse. David and Samuel the seer "…had appointed them to their positions of trust." (1 Chronicles 9:22) Standing guard at a doorway doesn't sound very comfy to me anyway. The word is trust.

You got it, baker. "The gatekeepers were stationed on the four sides: east, west, north, and south." (1 Chronicles 9:24) Every direction had gatekeepers standing at their posts. That's a whole lot of doorways covered, friend. So no side of the house of the LORD was left without a gatekeeper.

East is one of the sides, but it isn't the only one. The text says the gatekeepers "…were stationed on the four sides: east, west, north, and south." (1 Chronicles 9:24) So the answer is all four sides.

North is on the list, but it's only one of four. "The gatekeepers were stationed on the four sides: east, west, north, and south." (1 Chronicles 9:24) So the gatekeepers weren't gathered on a single side. The answer is all four sides.
That's it! Their relatives "…came from their villages at fixed times to serve with them for seven-day periods." (1 Chronicles 9:25) A week at a time on the job. Seven days is the answer, friend.
Forty days is a big number, so I see the pull. But here the relatives came in "…for seven-day periods." (1 Chronicles 9:25) That's one week at a time. So the answer is seven days.
Three months would be a long shift, friend! The text says the relatives came from their villages at fixed times to serve "…for seven-day periods." (1 Chronicles 9:25) So the answer is seven days.

explanations.answer: They guard it and open it each morning
explanations.explanation: Yes! The four chief gatekeepers spent the night around the house of God "…because they were responsible for guarding it and opening it every morning." (1 Chronicles 9:27) Guarding it and opening it were their jobs. I think that's one early alarm clock, and nobody could hit snooze on it.

explanations.answer: They have no homes of their own
explanations.explanation: The text never says that, so I won't add it. The reason it gives is that they "…were responsible for guarding it and opening it every morning." (1 Chronicles 9:27) Their job was guarding the house of God and opening it, so that's the answer.

explanations.answer: They are fasting for the feast
explanations.explanation: A fast isn't mentioned anywhere in these verses. The writer says they spent the night there "…because they were responsible for guarding it and opening it every morning." (1 Chronicles 9:27) The reason is the guarding and the opening.

True! Some of them were "…in charge of the articles used in worship, to count them whenever they were brought in or taken out." (1 Chronicles 9:28) Every item got counted going in and coming out. I'd have loved that system for my cookie cutters.

It's actually true, friend. The text says some of them were "…in charge of the articles used in worship, to count them whenever they were brought in or taken out." (1 Chronicles 9:28) So they counted the articles both coming in and going out.

Baking the bread! "A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with baking the bread." (1 Chronicles 9:31) Somebody was trusted to bake in the house of God, and I'm a little proud of the profession. Okay, a LOT proud.
Lamps are a good guess, but that's not what the verse says. Mattithiah the Levite "…was entrusted with baking the bread." (1 Chronicles 9:31) So the answer is baking the bread.
Basins would be a lot of scrubbing, friend, but they're not in this verse. It says Mattithiah the Levite "…was entrusted with baking the bread." (1 Chronicles 9:31) His job was baking the bread.

explanations.answer: They are on duty day and night
explanations.explanation: That's right. The musicians stayed in the temple chambers and "…were exempt from other duties because they were on duty day and night." (1 Chronicles 9:33) Music was their whole assignment. I think that's a lot of practicing.

The text doesn't say the king did anything here. The musicians were exempt from other duties "…because they were on duty day and night." (1 Chronicles 9:33) The reason given is their round-the-clock duty.

explanations.answer: Their families serve in their place
explanations.explanation: That's not in the text. The musicians "…were exempt from other duties because they were on duty day and night." (1 Chronicles 9:33) Nobody is said to be filling in for them, and the reason is simply that they were always on duty.
